questions.passage: Like his father, grandfather, and every male ancestor before him, Yoshi has lived his entire life there, cultivating rice and tea.
questions.prompt: Which statement best restates Yoshi’s connection with earlier generations?
options: He followed a family pattern in both place and occupation.
He returned to the town after years overseas.
He shared his ancestors’ birthplace but rejected their work.
He left farming to study family history.
analyses: A 把地点延续与职业延续合并改写，受到首尾句支持。
B 原文是 lived his entire life there，没有海外归来。
C rejected their work 与 cultivating rice and tea 及 followed the path 相反。
D 误把农业生活改为历史研究，且 left farming 与原文相反。

evidence.quote: Like his father, grandfather, and every male ancestor before him, Yoshi has lived his entire life there, cultivating rice and tea.

vocabulary.meaning: 耕作；种植（cultivate 的 -ing 形式）
vocabulary.context: 种植水稻与茶叶，说明 Yoshi 的日常生活
vocabulary.example: The family earns a living by cultivating rice.

vocabulary.context: 父系世代延续的生活路径
vocabulary.example: Her ancestors lived in the valley.

questions.passage: He chose this path after just a year of agricultural high school, when he dropped out to become a farmer.
questions.prompt: What did Yoshi do after about one year of agricultural high school?
options: He became a farmer.
He married a woman from his school.
He moved to a neighbouring town.
He joined a softball league professionally.
analyses: A become a farmer 是原文明示的去向。
B 妻子来自邻镇，不等于同校同学，结婚时间也不同。
C 来自邻镇的是妻子，不能把修饰对象换为 Yoshi。
D 原文是 neighborhood softball league，没有职业身份，也未置于退学后立即发生。

evidence.quote: He chose this path after just a year of agricultural high school, when he dropped out to become a farmer.

vocabulary.context: 读了一年农业高中后离校务农
vocabulary.example: He dropped out of the course to work full-time.

questions.passage: In making these choices, Yoshi followed the path laid out by his ancestors, connecting with them through common threads of not just blood, but occupation, place, expectations, and way of life.
questions.prompt: In “the path laid out by his ancestors”, what does “path” refer to?
options: The physical route from Kyushu to Tokyo.
A sequence of trips organised by neighbours.
A road connecting farms and hot springs.
An established way of living passed through the family.
analyses: A 去东京是作者的经历，不是 Yoshi 沿袭的道路。
B 邻里旅行只是生活活动之一，不能概括祖先的职业与期待。
C 把隐喻误读成公路；没有连接农场与温泉的路线说明。
D 对应世代的生活方式，包括职业、地点与期待。

questions.passage: In my fourth year of college, I got a scholarship from Rotary International to study abroad in Maine.
questions.prompt: What enabled the author to study abroad in Maine during college?
options: An invitation from his girlfriend in Boston.
A job with Japan’s Ministry of Education.
A place on a neighbourhood association trip.
A scholarship from Rotary International.
analyses: A Boston 关系发生在后面，未说是出国留学的邀请来源。
B Ministry of Education 是留学前职业计划，不是资助来源。
C 邻里协会旅行是父亲的活动。
D 与 scholarship from Rotary International 逐字对应。

evidence.quote: In my fourth year of college, I got a scholarship from Rotary International to study abroad in Maine.

questions.passage: I simply wanted to improve my English. Yet, I met a student from Korea and fell in love.
questions.prompt: What contrast is introduced by “Yet” in the account of the summer programme?
options: He wanted a relationship but decided to study instead.
He hoped only to improve his English but unexpectedly fell in love.
He disliked Boston but visited it for academic research.
He planned to stay in Tokyo but found a job in Maine.
analyses: A 把意愿与实际结果倒置。
B only 对应 simply，unexpectedly 对应 Yet 表示的意外转折。
C Boston 的出行目的是见她，不是学术研究；片段也没有 dislike。
D 没有在 Maine 找工作的情节。

evidence.quote: I simply wanted to improve my English. Yet, I met a student from Korea and fell in love.

vocabulary.context: 把只想学英语与意外恋爱连接起来
vocabulary.example: I wanted a quiet trip. Yet I made many new friends.

questions.translation: 我只是想提高英语水平。然而，我遇到了一位来自韩国的学生，并坠入爱河。

questions.passage: Before I started the program in Maine, I attended a summer English program on Staten Island in New York City. I had just broken up with my girlfriend in Tokyo and was tired of being in a relationship.
questions.prompt: What was the narrator's attitude towards relationships before the summer programme?
questions.promptZh: 参加暑期项目之前，叙述者对恋爱关系持什么态度？
options: He was planning to reunite with his former girlfriend.
He wanted his girlfriend in Tokyo to join him abroad.
He had recently ended a relationship and felt weary of it.
He decided that a relationship should replace studying abroad.
optionsZh: 他希望东京的女友与他一同出国。
他刚结束一段恋情，对恋爱关系感到疲惫。
他决定用恋爱代替出国学习。
analyses: A broken up 表示已经分手；本句没有复合计划。
B 句中女友在 Tokyo 是过去恋情的背景，没有邀请同行。
C had just broken up 对应刚结束恋情，was tired of being in a relationship 对应对恋爱感到疲惫。
D 原文描述感情状态，没有说他放弃或替换留学计划；也不能扩大成永久拒绝恋爱。

vocabulary.context: had just broken up 表示在叙述的那个过去时点之前刚与东京的女友分手。
vocabulary.example: They had broken up before he moved to another city.

questions.translation: 开始缅因州的课程之前，我在纽约市的斯塔滕岛参加了一个暑期英语课程。我刚与东京的女友分手，也厌倦了处于恋爱关系之中。

evidence.quote: I had just broken up with my girlfriend in Tokyo and was tired of being in a relationship.

questions.passage: She was about to start graduate school in Boston. I was about to start a year in Lewiston, Maine. During the 1991–1992 academic year, I took a Greyhound bus to Boston to see her every weekend. In May, I had to go back to Tokyo.
questions.prompt: What was the Korean student about to do?
questions.promptZh: 那位韩国学生即将做什么？
options: Begin graduate studies in Boston.
Start a year of study in Lewiston.
Return to Tokyo to finish college.
Take a job with Japan's Ministry of Education.
optionsZh: 在波士顿开始研究生学习。
在刘易斯顿开始一年的学习。
analyses: A She was about to start graduate school in Boston 明确给出她的计划。
B Lewiston 是叙述者接下来一年的所在地点，不能交换两人的去向。
C 回 Tokyo 是叙述者稍后五月的经历，不是这位学生的安排。
D 文部省工作是叙述者留学前的职业打算，不属于她。

vocabulary.meaning: 研究生院；研究生阶段学习
vocabulary.context: 说明她即将在 Boston 开始研究生教育，未指明具体大学或学位。
vocabulary.example: He plans to apply to graduate school next year.

questions.translation: 她即将在波士顿开始研究生学习。我则即将在缅因州刘易斯顿开始一年的生活。在 1991—1992 学年，我每个周末都乘灰狗巴士去波士顿看她。五月，我不得不回到东京。

evidence.quote: She was about to start graduate school in Boston.

questions.prompt: What did the narrator have to do in May?
questions.promptZh: 五月时，叙述者不得不做什么？
options: Move permanently to Chicago.
Begin graduate school in Boston.
Join an annual trip with his school friends.
Return to Tokyo.

参加与同学的年度旅行。

questions.passage: Though my career plan before studying abroad was to work for the Ministry of Education in Japan, and I hadn’t had any intention of attending graduate school in the U.S., by then I was determined to come back.
questions.prompt: What contrast is introduced by “Though” in the passage?
options: He always planned to study in the U.S., but eventually refused to return.
His earlier plans excluded U.S. graduate study, but he later wanted to return.
He intended to work in Tokyo and therefore never changed his plans.
His original goal was to work for the U.S. Ministry of Education.
questions.promptZh: 片段中的“Though”引出了什么对照？
optionsZh: 他一直计划赴美读研，最终却拒绝回去。
较早的计划没有赴美读研，但后来他决心返回。
他打算在东京工作，因此从未改变计划。
他原先的目标是在美国教育部工作。
analyses: A hadn’t had any intention 否定了早期赴美读研的意愿；结尾却是 determined to come back。
B 对齐原先在日本文部省工作且无意赴美读研，与后来决心返回的反差。
C 用 therefore 抹去了 Though 引出的转折；never 与决心改变不符。
D 原文是 Ministry of Education in Japan，地点被错换成美国。

evidence.quote: Though my career plan before studying abroad was to work for the Ministry of Education in Japan, and I hadn’t had any intention of attending graduate school in the U.S., by then I was determined to come back.

vocabulary.context: 与此前无意赴美读研形成转折，表明后来返回的意愿
vocabulary.example: She was determined to finish the course.

questions.translation: 虽然留学前，我的职业计划是在日本文部省工作，而且此前从未打算赴美读研究生，但到那时，我已经下定决心要回来。
